battlecards.why_selected: Signed national pricebook and rebate agreement delivering 16% savings while preserving technician familiarity with Carrier equipment.
battlecards.contract_terms: National price list effective 9/25/2025 – pricing frozen until written notice; incremental quarterly rebate (≈$297K/yr); no minimum volume commitment.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Threat of shifting volume to competing OEMs and consolidating spend; visibility of multi-brand spend profile gave pricing power.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Strong brand recognition, broad parts network, immediate availability.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Initial price book covered only 6 % of SKUs; higher list prices on parts prior to renegotiation.
battlecards.switching_costs: Field technician training, compatibility with existing installations, inventory of Carrier-specific parts.
key_contacts: Ben Cowles – Sr Director Finance (signatory, Carrier)
battlecards.notes: Agreement captured $22K front-end price reductions and $297K in rebates; focus now on monitoring quarterly spend to maximize rebate tier.

battlecards.why_selected: National Consolidator Incentive Program increased rebate from 6.5 % to 8 % on all Rheem purchases and standardized pricing across distributors.
battlecards.contract_terms: Consolidator Incentive Agreement effective 1/1/2026; rebate tiers scale 8 %–16 % based on enterprise Rheem spend; term aligned to full calendar year with optional renewal.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Ability to aggregate purchases from five business units to reach higher rebate tier; competitive offers from other OEMs.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Enterprise rebate structure, broad distributor network (Gemaire, Allied, Ferguson).
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Requires rigorous spend tracking to unlock higher tiers.
battlecards.switching_costs: Minimal – purchases continue through existing distributors; main effort is spend reporting to Rheem.
battlecards.notes: Projected incremental rebate gain of $106K versus status quo; onboarding in progress.

battlecards.why_selected: Offered back-to-dollar-one 16 % rebate (~$441K) and agreed to revisit front-end pricing gaps identified vs Daikin.
battlecards.contract_terms: Proposed rebate tiers: 16 % ($1-$8M), 18 % ($8-$15M), 20 % (>$15M); agreement pending final front-end price addendum.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Detailed SKU-level benchmark showed Lennox premiums; threat to migrate volume to competing OEMs.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Strong rebate economics, wide product line, existing install base.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Front-end pricing initially non-competitive on key SKUs.
battlecards.switching_costs: Moderate – would require retraining and stocking alternative brands.
battlecards.notes: Treya continuing to push for additional price concessions before execution.

battlecards.why_selected: Agreed to 2 % base + 5 % growth rebates on ECM spend without requiring national contract.
battlecards.contract_terms: Rebate applies to $355K ECM product family; growth rebate tied to volume uplift; quarterly true-up.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Proof of higher Daikin passthrough pricing put pressure on Johnstone to enhance rebate.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Local availability of ECM motors and parts.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Declined full national program; limited corporate governance.
battlecards.switching_costs: Low – category specific and interchangeable products.
battlecards.notes: Potential additional $259K claim under review but not yet confirmed.

battlecards.why_selected: Rampart GPO pricing delivered >40 % savings and allowed enterprise standardization under one provider.
battlecards.contract_terms: GPO master agreement; estimated 3-4-month rollout; pricing tied to negotiated Rampart tier, no location-specific contracts.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Ability to move 83 % of Cintas volume; consolidated headcount of ~300 techs.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Lower rental rates, simplified billing, GPO oversight.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Requires inventory transition and coordination across 7 business units.
battlecards.switching_costs: Return of Cintas garments, sizing events for staff, potential buy-out of remaining Cintas contract terms.
battlecards.notes: Implementation roadmap drafted; key to monitor local service quality during ramp-up.

battlecards.why_not_selected: Pricing 30-60 % higher than Unifirst GPO offer; multiple contract fragments across business units.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Threat of total volume loss led to limited concessions but still above GPO pricing.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Large footprint, established service at most locations.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: High rental rates, complex contract landscape, restocking fees.
battlecards.switching_costs: Early termination charges, garment return logistics.
battlecards.notes: Cintas may still be used for limited purchased uniforms where Unifirst has no coverage.

battlecards.why_selected: Competitive on core plumbing SKUs and agreed to hold national pricing with 30-day notice cap; 2 % 10-day early-pay discount added.
battlecards.contract_terms: MOU 1/20/2026 – 12/31/2026; standardized pricing (Exhibit I) with 30-day increase notice; margin cap tied to appendix.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Threat of shifting volume to Ferguson and others; consolidated demand forecast.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Inventory depth, willingness to fix pricing, payment discount.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Did not deliver net unit-price savings in Round 2; requires close audit of future increases.
battlecards.switching_costs: Low – commodity SKUs available at competitors.
battlecards.notes: Hughes remains primary for water heaters; monitor for price creep beyond 30-day notice.

battlecards.why_selected: Retained to avoid disruption on HVAC controls and filter lines; committed to revised price list in MOU.
battlecards.contract_terms: Draft MOU mirrors Hughes template; pricing subject to 30-day notice with evidence of manufacturer increases.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Competitive quotes from R.E. Michel produced price concessions on select SKUs.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Coverage on thermostat and UV equipment lines; existing logistics network.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Net price savings modest; SKU quote coverage only 38 % of RFP list.
battlecards.switching_costs: Moderate – would need to requalify thermostat SKUs.
battlecards.notes: Audit actual savings during first quarter of 2026.

battlecards.why_selected: Delivered the only positive unit-price savings in Round 2 ($25.9K) and agreed to adopt Treya target pricing on high-volume SKUs.
battlecards.contract_terms: MOU pending signature; pricing fixed through 12/31/2026 with quarterly review; no minimum volume.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Demonstrated SKU-level price gaps vs Hughes and Dynamic Air.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Competitive on controls and copper fittings, reliable fill rates.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Limited quote coverage (14 % of SKUs); needs improvement in inventory breadth.

battlecards.why_not_selected: Small savings and limited SKU overlap; retained only for proprietary UV products on an as-needed basis.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Low due to niche product specialization.
battlecards.switching_costs: High for proprietary RM2-series lamps; otherwise low.

battlecards.why_not_selected: Failed to submit complete proposal in time for final analysis; would need significant price reductions to be competitive.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Potential future volume carrot if willing to meet target pricing.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: National distribution footprint, strong plumbing assortment.

summary.skipped_reason: Suppliers with only basic spend data or simple renewals (e.g., Interplay Learning, P-Card banks) were skipped.

extraction_notes: Baseline and savings figures taken from project summary tables and RFP analysis workbooks.
Where negative or unclear savings occurred (Hughes, Baker), savings fields were left null to avoid mis-representation.
Contract details for Hughes Supply sourced from signed MOU dated 1/20/2026.
